\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for to sniff, then the Russian for to touch.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{фотографировать}}
\textbf{\ru{фотографировать}} (\emph{fotografírovat}) — \textquotedblleft{}to photograph\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{фотографировать}} is \emph{\ru{фотография}}, \textquotedblleft{}a photograph\textquotedblright{}, made a verb with \emph{-\ru{ировать}}: Greek \emph{phōs}, \textquotedblleft{}light\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{gráphein}, \textquotedblleft{}to write\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

Before the new one: say the Russian for to photograph, then the Russian for to gather.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{обещать}}
\textbf{\ru{обещать}} (\emph{obeshchát}) — \textquotedblleft{}to promise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{обещать}} — taken from Church Slavonic, says Vasmer, in place of an Old Russian \emph{*\ru{обечати}}; the \emph{-\ru{щ}-} marks it. It goes with \emph{\ru{обет}}, \textquotedblleft{}a vow\textquotedblright{}, on the old root \emph{\ru{вет}-}, \textquotedblleft{}counsel, word\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
